_about.purpose: Architecture facts for the seven candidate models, used by vram_model.py and planner.html.

confidence.sourced: stated explicitly by at least one retrieved source (see 'src')
confidence.derived: computed from sourced numbers by an identity stated in notes.md
confidence.estimated: reasoned from the model class; correct to roughly +/-20%
confidence.unverified: single weak source or internally contradictory; do not trust without measuring

_about.note: huggingface.co was blocked by this session's egress policy, so no config.json or GGUF header could be read directly. Every number below is traceable to 'src' or flagged.
_about.expert_split_identity: For MoE: expert_total = (P_total - P_active) / (1 - k/n_experts); non_expert = P_total - expert_total. This is exact given P_total, P_active, k, n, so the per-token byte counts are right even where the physical tensor split differs.

gpu.name: NVIDIA RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB (AD106)
gpu.usable_note: ~15.0 GiB assumed free for llama.cpp; a desktop compositor takes 0.5-1.0 GiB. Headless/WSL can reclaim most of it.
gpu.pcie: Gen4 x8 card in a Z170 Gen3 x16 slot => Gen3 x8 = 7.88 GB/s effective

cpu.name: Intel i5-6600K (Skylake, 4C/4T)
cpu.isa: AVX2 + FMA, no AVX-512, no AMX
cpu.ram_note: DDR4-3200 dual channel = 51.2 GB/s theoretical; 4 Skylake cores realistically sustain 55-70% of that

defaults.eff_gpu_note: fraction of theoretical VRAM bandwidth llama.cpp reaches on batch-1 matvec; 0.75-0.85 is typical on Ada
defaults.eff_cpu_note: 4 Skylake cores cannot saturate dual-channel DDR4-3200; includes Q4 dequant overhead
defaults.cpu_thread_note: KEY FINDING: llama.cpp's CPU-side MoE FFN on AVX2 Skylake sustains only ~2.2 GB/s of quantised weights per core (dequantise + GEMV, no AVX-512/AMX). With 4 threads that is ~8.8 GB/s -- far BELOW the 28 GB/s the DDR4-3200 subsystem could deliver. So on this box the CPU offload path is CORE-bound, not RAM-bound. Faster RAM would not help; fewer offloaded bytes would. Calibrate with bench.sh.
defaults.mtp_note: Upside only. A GGUF shipping MTP tensors does not mean llama.cpp implements self-speculation for that architecture -- support is per-architecture and often absent (cf. the LM Studio 'Nemotron MTP not detected' report). Default assumption is 1.0x; verify with bench.sh before counting on it.
defaults.overhead_note: kernel launch + per-layer CPU<->GPU sync. Hybrid figure from typical -ncmoe behaviour; calibratable.

gated attention, GQA 24/4, head_dim 256 with a 64-dim rotary slice

global layers. The reported ~74% KV reduction vs an all-global 60-layer model is accounted for by the 50 SWA layers, not by an extra sharing factor - adding both double-counts. n_kv x head_dim = 2048 DERIVED from the reported ~22 GiB at 262k.
